end.summary: Placed 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 CE, and 1947 CE in chronological order once.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ordering BCE and CE dates on a timeline and identifying archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources. Aarav used the helpful method of counting BCE years down towards 1 BCE and placed the dates correctly in sequence. They mixed up the idea that an older inscription or a single book must always be completely true; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen: false). At home, ask Aarav to compare two sources about one event and note what each source can and cannot tell us.
